reviewer: Claude (maintainer-requested review of PR #77 and follow-up fixes)
summary: Reviewed the whole PR against its merge-base and fixed four issues found in it. (1) The required PR check ran only the checker as changed by the PR, so a PR could weaken its own gate, and the trusted workflow_run recheck cannot be a required PR check: threat-model.yml now also runs the base commit's checker (separate worktree, python -I, no secrets) against the candidate objects. (2) workflow_run receives Actions secrets for fork PRs and ran regardless of CI result: the advisory job now runs only for same-repository PRs after a successful CI and skips Dependabot. (3) Dependabot PRs could never pass because they cannot carry a record: --dependency-update (set by CI only when the GitHub event names dependabot[bot] as PR author) exempts changes limited to dependency manifests and workflow uses: lines; anything else still fails. (4) Control flow per AGENTS.md: unknown refs are checked with rev-parse --quiet and reported instead of raised, acceptance dates are validated without exceptions, remaining except clauses carry exception-ok reasons, the advisory default output uses the platform temp directory. The threat selftest cleared PATH and its redirect server answered before reading the body, so it failed on Windows; both fixed. ADR-0047 (still proposed), the design document and AGENTS.md describe the base-checker gate, the fork restriction and the Dependabot path.

findings.evidence: threat-model.yml checked out the PR head and ran that head's tools/security/review.py; the default-branch recheck in threat-review.yml is a workflow_run and cannot be selected as a required PR status.
findings.resolution: Second step runs the checker from a worktree of the PR base commit against the candidate objects; bootstrap case (no checker in base) is logged explicitly.

findings.evidence: threat-review.yml ran for every pull_request workflow_run, including forks and failed CI, with SKIRNIR_SECURITY_AI_KEY in the environment once configured.
findings.resolution: Job condition requires conclusion success, head_repository equal to this repository and an actor other than dependabot[bot]; covered in design document and ADR-0047.

findings.evidence: Every Dependabot PR would fail the evidence check: Dependabot cannot write docs/security/reviews/current.json and a pushed record stops Dependabot from rebasing.
findings.resolution: check --dependency-update limits the exemption to go.mod/go.sum/requirements*.txt and workflow uses: lines; CI sets it only from github.event.pull_request.user.login; tests cover accepted and rejected cases.

findings.evidence: review.py derived missing refs and invalid dates from CalledProcessError/ValueError and had except clauses without exception-ok reasons (AGENTS.md control-flow rules); selftest_threat_review.py failed 3 tests on Windows (cleared PATH, unread request body).
findings.resolution: Refs and dates checked beforehand, remaining boundaries marked, tests keep PATH/SYSTEMROOT and read the body; 18/18 pass on Windows and Linux.

findings.evidence: The record still proves freshness and shape only; a dishonest author can write a false record.
findings.resolution: Unchanged baseline risk documented in the register and design; maintainer review remains required.

limitations: The threat model documents (English and German) and the risk register were checked for structure, referenced paths and privacy, not re-derived scenario by scenario.

The base-checker step and the workflow_run conditions are verified by reading and YAML parsing only; they run for the first time in GitHub Actions. This PR is the bootstrap case: its base has no checker, so the base-checker step only logs that.
The Dependabot exemption trusts GitHub's PR author field; the maintainer still has to review each dependency bump.
No real model endpoint, repository ruleset or live CI schedule was exercised.
